sources.title: Row-permutation and softmax derivation
sources.details: Each candidate row x_j=[CLS,state,SEP,question,SEP,meaning_j] is processed by the same f_theta. Embedding/positions depend on columns, LayerNorm on the final feature axis, and SDPA on positions within a row; no operation reduces across rows. For a row permutation P, f_theta(PX)=P f_theta(X). Softmax(Pz)_j=exp(z_(Pj))/sum_k exp(z_(Pk))=(P softmax(z))_j since P preserves the multiset. The proof is for the same candidate meanings/set and deterministic scoring; finite-precision kernels may differ within rounding tolerance, and adding/removing a candidate changes the denominator. Semantic-ID tie selection uses min((-p,id)), so ties do not depend on list index.

sources.title: Why task-specific labels and single-answer criteria matter
sources.details: For info, available=sum(required field present); yes iff available=len(REQUIRED[task]); grade2 iff all, otherwise grade0 iff zero, else grade1. With address REQUIRED=(), information is sufficient without an application number; card needs application. For categorical CE L=-log p_y, two incompatible equally valid labels for the same fully observed input cannot both attain zero loss: p_a=p_b=1 violates sum p=1. Thus a single-answer task requires an unambiguous criterion, or labels/objective must be changed; this is a task-contract recommendation, not a claim that real multi-answer tasks do not exist.

sources.title: Concentration does not identify correctness
sources.details: c=(n*p_max-1)/(n-1) only uses the distribution. Holding the same p and changing which semantic answer is true leaves c unchanged. The preserved weather example has argmax boxes but goldnone. Hence c close to1 cannot logically entail correctness, and zero errors on one finite sample cannot rule out errors on another distribution.
